DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 91 s. 2021 JUL 19 202! DIR. JOSEPHINE CABRIDO-LEYSA Regional Director, DILG-Region XII Prime Regional Government Center Carpenter Hill, Koronadal City Dear RD Cabrido-Leysa: This has reference to your letter dated 09 June 2021 requesting legal opinions on the following issues: 1. Pending the designation from SILG of the highest ranking sangguniang bayan member as Acting Vice Mayor, what will be his official designation? Can the highest ranking sanggunian member approve/sign disbursements involving regularly recurring administrative expenses such as payroll for employees and expenses for light and water, telephone and other utility and telecommunication services? 2. In the Administrative Order No. 015 issued by Hon. Suharto Mangudadatu, PhD, Govemor of the Province of Sultan Kudarat, Section 4 thereof states that the next highest ranking member of the Sangguniang Bayan of Isulan shall automatically exercise the duties and functions of the Office of the Municipal Vice-Mayor, including the power to appoint, suspend or dismiss employees. Would this constitute that the highest ranking sangguniang bayan member can now be elevated to the position as Acting Vice Mayor and perform the duties and functions of the Office of the Municipal Vice Mayor despite the pending designation process required in DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2019-21? 3. In the filling-up of temporary vacancies, are the appointees of SILG entitled to receive the salaries and other benefits as Acting Sangguniang Bayan Members? Per the documents submitted to the Central Office, it appears that on 17 May 2021, Governor Suharto Mangudadatu issued Administrative Order No. 15, series of 2021 imposing upon Vice-Mayor Lord Dean Castillo and five (5) other members of the Sangguniang Bayan of Isulan, Sultan

Kudarat, a 45-day preventive suspension by virtue of an administrative case filed against them before the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, that province. On the same day, the order was implemented and served upon the vice mayor and the SB members. On 31 May 2021, the documents for the appointment of the highest- ranking SB member and the SK Federation Vice-President were forwarded to the Central Office for designation of those positions temporarily vacated pursuant to DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2019-21 and A) 15, series of 2018, entitled "AUTHORIZING THE SECRETARY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT (DILG) OR THE OFFICER-IN-CHARGE (OIC) TO FILL TEMPORARY VACANCIES IN CERTAIN LOCAL ELECTIVE OFFICES TO PREVENT HIATUS IN AND PARALYSIS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT OPERATIONS". Hence, your aforesaid letter requesting for legal opinion. Meantime, DILG-Region XII has these initial positions on the above- enumerated issues: 1. As to the first and second issues, you are of the view that the next highest ranking sanggunian member may assume the Office of the Vice-Mayor pending designation by the SILG to prevent hiatus in the Office—the very reason why Administrative Order No. 15, series of 2018 was issued by the Office of the President. You based your position on Item VI (1) of DILG MC 2019-21 which provides: "I. Pending the completion of selection and designation processes referred to in the immediately preceding sections, the remaining local elective official/s shall administer the day-to-day operations of the concerned local government unit to ensure continuous and effective delivery of public services therein;" 2. As to the third query, you are of the view that the members who are to assume by reason of succession may claim RATA but not the salary of the suspended members. Their assumption being part of the duties they were sworn to perform as elective officials. As to designated by the SILG other than those referred to in the immediately preceding paragraph, however, they added that the designated officials may claim the RATA and may be entitled to honorarium (not salary) equivalent to the salaries received by

the other SB members in gratitude for the services they have rendered. In reply to the first issue you posed, while we support your initial view that the highest ranking sanggunian member may assume the Office of the Vice-Mayor pending designation by the SILG, the primary legal basis would be Section 344 of RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 , which reads: "Section 344. Certification, and Approval of, Vouchers. - No money shall be disbursed unless the local budget officer certifies to the existence of appropriation that has been legally made for the purpose, the local accountant has obligated said appropriation, and the local treasurer certifies to the availability of funds for the purpose. Vouchers and payrolls shall be certified to and approved by the head of the department or office who has administrative control of the fund concerned. as to validity. propriety. and legality of the claim involved. Except in cases of disbursements involving regularly recurring administrative expenses such as payrolls for regular or permanent employees, expenses for light, water, telephone and telegraph services, remittances to government creditor agencies such as GSIS, SSS, LDP, DBP, National Printing Office, Procurement Service of the DBM and others, approval of the disbursement voucher by the local chief executive himself shall be required whenever local funds are disbursed. In cases of special or trust funds, disbursements shall be approved by the administrator of the fund. In case of temporary absence or incapacity of the department head or chief of office. the officer next-in-rank shall automatically perform his function and he shall be fully responsible therefor." (Emphasis Supplied) As to the second issue, Section 4 of Administrative Order No. 015 issued by Governor Mangudadatu which states that the next highest ranking member of the Sangguniang Bayan of Isulan shall automatically exercise the duties and functions of the Office of the Municipal Vice-Mayor, including the power to appoint, suspend or dismiss employees, appears to be inconsistent with AO 15, series of 2018 issued by the Office of the President and MC 2019-21 issued by this Department which both provide that a designation issued by the President, through the SILG or the OIC- DILG, is necessary before the highest ranking sanggunian member could assume as acting provincial vice-governor or city or municipal vice-mayor. In fact, Item IV (E)(6) requires and we quote: "6. The designated official/s shall enter upon the discharge of their duties only after having been issued their corresponding designations and after having

taken the requisite oaths of office before any of the officers who have the general authority to administer oaths pursuant to existing laws, rules and regulations." Hence, Governor Mangudadatu is hereby enjoined to make his issuance consistent with the issuances of the Office of the President and this Department. As to the third issue, we find the initial position of DILG-Region XII in order. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. Please be guided accordingly. Very truly yours, BY THE AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: GAN Underse tary for Local Government Ls/17
